players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Seventy-somethings, a 21-point drubbing and an army of regretful Haaland captains: GW1 served up chaos
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 arrived like a pub quiz question nobody studied for. We had a proper shootout (72-71), a 21-point thumping, an honourable draw where neither manager deserved praise, and more managers doubling down on Erling Haaland than is strictly sensible. Grab a drink — this one’s for the WhatsApp savagery.

matches.title: Richard 56 - 57 Prince Majid Rd FC (Rich v Rami)
matches.text: Tiny margins, big feelings. Rich lost by one to Rami after both sides leaned on similar ingredients: João Pedro popped up with 11 for both sides and Bruno as captain (Rich and Rami both handed him the armband and got the exact same 4 points). Rich will tell you it was agonising; Rami will tell you it was worth every Riyal. One-point defeats are the worst because they’re too close to accept it was bad luck and too far to blame the fixtures.

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 - 71 Roped in again (Rob v Paul)
matches.text: If you like drama, this was your match. Rob edged Paul by a single point in the highest-scoring fixture of the week — 143 points between them. Rob’s Bruno captain did its 4-point thing again, Woollyjamin White and João Pedro chipped in nicely, and Paul somehow managed 71 and still left the pitch dejected. Paul: 71 points and a loss. The rest of us: pocket calculators out, checking whether consolation prizes exist.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 - 76 Bielsa's Babes (Dave v Paddy)
matches.text: Patrick marched to the highest score of the week (76) and made it look annoyingly tidy. Big contributors across the pitch and the usual João Pedro/Ødegaard/Woollyjamin White combo did the business. David’s 67 is nothing to sniff at — but Patrick’s total means David gets to moan about 'what might have been' while Patrick enjoys being top of the league for approximately 48 hours.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 - 51 BeLucky Again (Tom v Kev)
matches.text: Tom produced the week’s lowest score (47), which, knowing Tom, will be blamed on Spursy fate rather than selection. Kev, probably half a bunker away while making his transfers, managed a 51 and the win — fair play. Tom did at least have Marc Guéhi’s 10, which is the kind of consolation you pair with a muttered 'should’ve watched the team sheet earlier.'

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 - 50 Seattle Scorchers (Watson v Crystal)
matches.text: A draw so boring it's almost polite. Both teams finished on 50, which is the kind of symmetry mathematicians enjoy and managers hate. Rob and Andrew both had João Pedro on 11 and captained Haaland to 4 — the identical totals mean nobody can sneer at the other for being worse. It’s a shared, low-key misery.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 - 59 Atletico Waspo (Dunne v Woolly Foster)
matches.text: Woolly Foster took the win with 59 while James managed 55; both had decent returns from João Pedro and a mixed bag elsewhere. Nothing spectacular, nothing catastrophic — just the sort of solid start Woolly will bottle if he remembers to tee off early on Saturday.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 - 50 Turf Less (Woolly v Bradshaw)
matches.text: Woolly unleashed the widest margin of the week (21) and left Bradshaw wondering how 50 felt like losing by a country mile. Woolly’s side hit 71 and made it look easy enough that you suspect money was involved — or multiple subscriptions. Bradshaw had Cole Palmer’s good 13 and Morgan Rogers’ 8, but it wasn’t nearly enough. Burnley-related jokes are always available, but this was just a straightforward outscore.

awards.winner: Humorous Name United v Roped in again (Rob / Paul)
awards.text: 72-71. The highest-scoring match and the thriller of the round. Full credit to both for making the group chat combust.

awards.award: The Couldn’t Ask for More (Except a Win) Award
awards.text: Scored 71 and still lost. That is the sort of performance that should come with a consolation pint and a therapist on speed dial.

awards.award: The Haaland Roulette (Everyone Lost the Spin) Award
awards.text: A suspicious number of you doubled Haaland and earned 4 points. List includes Patrick, Woolly, Woolly Foster, Kevin, David, James, Watson, and Paul. Fickle little bugger, isn’t he.
Biggest winning margin of the week (21) and a tidy 71. Woolbrohampton made it look like an investment round that actually paid out.

1.table_commentary: The official Super 8s table — using H2H points and FPL tie-breakers — has Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) on top with 76, Rob second with 72 and Woolbrohampton third on 71. Woolly Foster’s Atletico Waspo and Rami’s Prince Majid Rd FC round out the top five. Kev is quietly sixth with a win (probably while playing golf), Watson and Crystal sit in the polite mid-table with that 50-50 draw, and Tom (el Guapo) is rock bottom with 47 — a position guaranteed to produce at least one dramatic transfer and several explanations involving Spurs.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) v Woolbrohampton (Woolly)
preview.text: Rami scraped a one-point win this week while Woolly delivered the biggest margin. This looks like a proper test: Woolly will fancy another high total after a 71, and Rami will be hoping his away-from-the-Saudi-watch run continues. Expect João Pedro to feature again and for both managers to overthink exactly one bench move each.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes (Paddy) v Humorous Name United (Rob)
preview.text: Top-of-the-table clash — Patrick already has the weekend’s highest score and Rob was involved in the 72-71 thriller. Both teams score, both teams pick similar big-hitters; probably more entertaining for neutrals than for the managers who have to explain captaincy choices afterwards.

Paul’s 71 last week and Rich’s 56 make this one easy to headline: likely high-scoring and nervy. Paul will be desperate to convert a huge score into actual H2H points; Rich will want revenge after losing by a single goal the last time he faced a tight result. Could be fireworks or more quiet, stubborn point-gathering — either way it’ll give the rest of us content for the chat.

1.closing: That’s your GW1: a lovely mess of close calls and one-sided affairs. Take the good bits, hide the captain decisions you made at 10pm on deadline night, and I’ll see you for more excuses and wagers next week.
